correctness.rationale: From the explicit circuit and accepted equal-sign measurement outcomes, averaging independent erased controlled-Z phases yields a 16-state replica transfer T with entry (2p-1)^D and parity projectors P0/P1. Two-step sector A_ef=P_f T P_e T P_f has rank one with simple eigenvalue 64 at p=0, others zero. Independently rebuilt its 16x16 exact integer derivatives and obtained eigen Taylor coefficients -384p and quadratic 1536 (00), 1280 (01,10), 1088 (11), including 16 noiseless endpoint contractions. Eigenvalue ratios yield log(-)=-4p^2 and -7p^2; multiplying n/2 gives the e^{-2c} and e^{-7c/2} limits with a uniform perturbative gap. The resulting Bell-diagonal partial transpose gives negativity threshold; acceptance has leading log(lambda00/64)=-6p, hence -3c when p*n*p^2 bounded. Original physical verifier independently brute-propagates all 256 erasure patterns and four accepted records for n=2, but this is not a proof of the infinite limit. Exact n/p domains and rare acceptance are preserved.

value.rationale: An apparently length-independent first noise derivative could suggest indefinite robustness. The nontrivial n~p^{-2} scaling, exact entanglement death threshold, and exponentially rare heralding resolve this natural operational misconception with a complete quantitative phase law, not merely an arbitrary finite graph benchmark.

final_claim: For parity-postselected extraction of a terminal two-qubit graph state from an even-length double-rail graph with independently omitted CZ gates of probability p, the conditional state has a full weak-noise limit along n*p^2->c: off-diagonal dephasings e^{-2c} or e^{-7c/2}. Fidelity is (1+2e^{-2c}+e^{-7c/2})/4; negativity max(0,(2e^{-2c}+e^{-7c/2}-1)/4), with unique threshold c≈0.458661867647; heralding has p*log P_acc -> -3c at positive finite c. If n*p^2 diverges, the corrected state tends I_4/4.
